publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: These anyons can be used to perform universal quantum computation.

span.label: anyonic excitations in two-dimensional lattice spin models
span.quote: Excitations in this model are anyons, meaning that the global wavefunction acquires some phase factor when one excitation moves around the other.

span.label: theoretical-construction
span.quote: From now on, we are constructing and studying nonabelian anyons which will allow universal quantum computation.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A PHYSICAL SYSTEM IS RE-DESCRIBED AS A COMPUTER, AND THE RE-DESCRIPTION IS MARKED AS ONE: a two-dimensional quantum system with anyonic excitations CAN BE CONSIDERED AS a quantum computer, with unitary transformations performed BY MOVING THE EXCITATIONS AROUND EACH OTHER and measurements BY JOINING EXCITATIONS IN PAIRS. `Can be considered as` is a way of regarding, not an identity, and the whole paper rests on it
span.quote: A two-dimensional quantum system with anyonic excitations can be considered as a quantum computer. Unitary transformations can be performed by moving the excitations around each other. Measurements can be performed by joining excitations in pairs and observing the result of fusion.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A PROPERTY IS LOCATED IN THE PHYSICS RATHER THAN IN THE PROTOCOL: such computation is said to be FAULT-TOLERANT BY ITS PHYSICAL NATURE - so what is elsewhere achieved by a procedure is here claimed as a feature of the material. The same word, fault-tolerance, is being attached to a different kind of thing
span.quote: Such computation is fault-tolerant by its physical nature. A quantum computer can provide fast solution for certain computational problems (e.g. factoring and discrete logarithm [1]) which require exponential time on an ordinary computer.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A PHYSICAL PROCESS IS RE-DESCRIBED AS AN ALGORITHM AND THE HEDGE IS LEFT IN: the spins' mutual interaction forcing a flipped spin back is said to be QUITE SIMILAR TO THE STANDARD ERROR CORRECTION PROCEDURE FOR THE REPETITION CODE, after which - WE MAY SAY THAT ERRORS ARE BEING CORRECTED AT THE PHYSICAL LEVEL. The identification is offered as a manner of speaking
span.quote: If some spin flips to the opposite direction, the interaction forces it to flip back to the direction of other spins. This process is quite similar to the standard error correction procedure for the repetition code. We may say that errors are being corrected at the physical level.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE ARGUMENT PROCEEDS BY ASKING WHY AN EXISTING PRACTICE IS UNNECESSARY: classical computation CAN ALSO be performed fault-tolerantly, HOWEVER IT IS RARELY DONE IN PRACTICE BECAUSE CLASSICAL GATES ARE RELIABLE ENOUGH - and the next sentence is WHY IS IT POSSIBLE. The paper's question is generated by noticing that a technique is available and unused
span.quote: Needless to say, classical computation can be also performed fault-tolerantly. However, it is rarely done in practice because classical gates are reliable enough. Why is it possible?

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE EXPLANATION IS SOUGHT IN THE EASIEST CASE FIRST AND THE CHOICE IS ANNOUNCED: LET US TRY TO UNDERSTAND THE EASIEST THING - why classical information can be stored reliably on magnetic media - before the quantum case is attempted. The order of explanation is stated rather than left implicit, and the chosen starting point is a fact about ordinary technology
span.quote: Let us try to understand the easiest thing — why classical information can be stored reliably on a magnetic media. Magnetism arise from spins of individual atoms. Each spin is quite sensitive to thermal fluctuations.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A THRESHOLD IS REPORTED AS THE OBSTACLE, AND ITS SIZE IS WHAT MATTERS RATHER THAN ITS EXISTENCE: an arbitrary circuit CAN be simulated with imperfect gates PROVIDED they are close to ideal up to a constant precision - and UNFORTUNATELY THE THRESHOLD VALUE IS RATHER SMALL, IT IS VERY DIFFICULT TO ACHIEVE THIS PRECISION. The theoretical solution is granted and then declared impractical by a number
span.quote: An arbitrary quantum circuit can be simulated using imperfect gates, provided these gates are close to the ideal ones up to a constant precision δ. Unfortunately, the threshold value of δ is rather small1; it is very difficult to achieve this precision.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A PROBLEM IS DECLARED SOLVED FROM ONE STANDPOINT AND OPEN FROM ANOTHER, WITH BOTH NAMED: physical realization is A BIG CHALLENGE and decoherence is one important problem - but FROM THE PURELY THEORETICAL POINT OF VIEW, THIS PROBLEM HAS BEEN SOLVED. Solved and unsolved at once, distinguished by which standpoint the word is being used from
span.quote: Physical realization of a quantum computer is a big challenge for scientists. One important problem is decoherence and systematic errors in unitary transformations which occur in real quantum systems. From the purely theoretical point of view, this problem has been solved due to Shor’s discovery of fault-tolerant quantum computation [2], with subsequent improvements

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AN EXPLICIT CAUTION AGAINST CONFLATING TWO THINGS THE SAME MATHEMATICS DESCRIBES: the local operators SHOULD NOT BE INTERPRETED AS symmetry transformations - the true symmetry transformations are a different set, and MATHEMATICALLY THEY ARE DESCRIBED BY THE SAME ALGEBRA, BUT THEIR ACTION ON PHYSICAL STATES IS DIFFERENT. One formalism, two referents, and the paper stops to say so
span.quote: Caution. The local operators should not be interpreted as symmetry transformations. The true symmetry transformations, so-called topological operators, will be defined in Sec. 6. Mathematically, they are described by the same algebra , but their action on physical states is different.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A TERM OF ART IS CONCEDED AND THEN SET ASIDE AS NOT THE RELEVANT PROPERTY: ONE MAY SAY that these codes have QUITE POOR PARAMETERS, and WELL, THEY ARE NOT GOOD CODES IN THE SENSE OF a cited definition - HOWEVER the code corrects almost any multiple error of a stated size, SO THESE CODES WORK. The established criterion is granted, and then shown not to be the criterion that matters here
span.quote: One may say that the toric codes have quite poor parameters. Well, they are not “good” codes in the sense of [17]. However, the code TOR(k) corrects almost any multiple error of size O(k2). (The constant factor in O(. . .) is related to the percolation problem). So, these codes work if the error rate is constant

span.label: real quantum systems suffer decoherence and systematic errors
span.note: what this limits: every fault-tolerance claim: DECOHERENCE AND SYSTEMATIC ERRORS IN UNITARY TRANSFORMATIONS OCCUR IN REAL QUANTUM SYSTEMS
span.quote: decoherence and systematic errors in unitary transformations which occur in real quantum systems

span.label: For the abelian toric-code memory the author has no way to read information into or out of the protected space.
span.note: what this limits: the abelian toric-code memory as a usable memory: UNFORTUNATELY, I DO NOT KNOW ANY WAY THIS QUANTUM INFORMATION CAN GET IN OR OUT
span.quote: Unfortunately, I do not know any way this quantum information can get in or out.

span.label: The gate set obtainable by braiding abelian anyons is not universal.
span.note: what this limits: any universality claim for braiding abelian anyons: TOO FEW THINGS CAN BE DONE BY MOVING ABELIAN ANYONS
span.quote: Too few things can be done by moving abelian anyons.

span.label: The group used for the universal-computation construction is physically implausible.
span.note: what this limits: the universal-computation construction: (THE GROUP S5 IS QUITE UNREALISTIC FOR PHYSICAL IMPLEMENTATION)
span.quote: (The group S5 is quite unrealistic for physical implementation).

span.label: No general theory underlies the constructions given.
span.note: what this limits: the generality of the constructions: A GENERAL THEORY OF ANYONS AND TOPOLOGICAL QUANTUM ORDER IS LACKING
span.quote: A general theory of anyons and topological quantum order is lacking.

span.label: The universal-computation results are stated without full derivation, to appear elsewhere.
span.note: what this limits: the universal-computation results as presented here: (THIS SECTION SHOULD BE CONSIDERED AS AN ABSTRACT OF RESULTS TO BE PRESENTED ELSEWHERE)
span.quote: (This section should be considered as an abstract of results to be presented elsewhere).

span.label: The number the whole fault-tolerance argument depends on is declared unknown in a footnote, with estimates three orders of magnitude apart.
span.note: what this limits: any use of the fault-tolerance threshold cited here: a footnote states the threshold is not known and that published estimates vary across several orders of magnitude
span.quote: Actually, the threshold is not known. Estimates vary from 1/300 [7] to 10−6 [4]

span.label: The case that errors can be corrected by physics rather than by procedure is made by analogy with magnetic storage, and hedged.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that this scheme corrects errors at the physical level: the supporting argument is an analogy with spins on magnetic media, which the author introduces with 'we may say'
span.quote: This process is quite similar to the standard error correction procedure for the repetition code. We may say that errors are being corrected at the physical level

span.label: The protection is degeneracy of a ground state on a surface, so the quantity protected depends on the topology chosen.
span.note: what this limits: the amount of protected quantum information claimed here: the protected space is the ground state of the Hamiltonian and is 4g-fold degenerate, where g is the genus of the surface the lattice is placed on
span.quote: The ground state of this Hamiltonian coincides with the protected space of the code. It is 4g-fold degenerate, where g is the genus of the surface

span.label: protected space
span.quote: The ground state of this Hamiltonian coincides with the protected space of the code

span.label: ground state
span.quote: The ground state of this Hamiltonian coincides with the protected space of the code. It is 4g-fold degenerate, where g is the genus of the surface

span.label: stabilizer operators
span.quote: we need a quantum code with local stabilizer operators

span.label: anyonic excitations
span.quote: A two-dimensional quantum system with anyonic excitations can be considered as a quantum computer

span.label: fault-tolerant
span.quote: Such computation is fault-tolerant by its physical nature

span.label: fault tolerance - BY PHYSICS RATHER THAN BY PROCEDURE: Shor's construction simulates a circuit with imperfect gates given a precision threshold, whereas here the computation is said to be fault-tolerant by its physical nature, so the two uses of the phrase name a software guarantee and a property of a material
span.quote: Such computation is fault-tolerant by its physical nature

span.label: the threshold - A NUMBER THE ARGUMENT NEEDS AND NOBODY HAS: the text calls it rather small and very difficult to achieve, and the footnote says outright that it is not known, giving estimates that differ by orders of magnitude
span.quote: Unfortunately, the threshold value of δ is rather small1; it is very difficult to achieve this precision

span.label: the protected space - AS A DEGENERATE GROUND STATE: it coincides with the ground state of a Hamiltonian built from local stabilizer operators, and its size is set by the genus of the surface rather than by anything about the computation
span.quote: The ground state of this Hamiltonian coincides with the protected space of the code. It is 4g-fold degenerate, where g is the genus of the surface

span.label: builds-on → quantum error-correcting codes (stabilizer codes)
span.quote: we need a quantum code with local stabilizer operators

span.label: builds-on → stabilizer quantum codes on lattices on the torus and other 2-D surfaces [6, 8]
span.quote: I start with a class of stabilizer quantum codes associated with lattices on the torus and other 2-D surfaces [6, 8].

span.label: extends → G. Castagnoli and M. Rasetti's use of one-dimensional anyons for quantum computation [14]
span.quote: An attempt to use one-dimensional anyons for quantum computation was made by G. Castagnoli and M. Rasetti [14], but the question of fault-tolerance was not considered.

span.label: builds-on → Einarsson's proof that ground state degeneracy on the torus follows from the existence of anyons [19]
span.quote: Here is the original Einarsson’s proof applied to our two types of particles.

span.label: protected space —same-as→ ground state
span.quote: The ground state of this Hamiltonian coincides with the protected space of the code

span.label: anyonic excitations —causes→ fault-tolerant
span.quote: A two-dimensional quantum system with anyonic excitations can be considered as a quantum computer. Unitary transformations can be performed by moving the excitations around each other. Measurements can be performed by joining excitations in pairs and observing the result of fusion. Such computation is fault-tolerant by its physical nature

span.label: 4g-fold — ground-state degeneracy of the toric-code Hamiltonian, g = genus of the surface
span.quote: It is 4g-fold degenerate, where g is the genus of the surface.

span.label: ΔE = 2 — energy gap separating excited states (eigenvalue difference of the stabilizer operators)
span.quote: All excited states are separated by an energy gap ∆E 2, because the difference between the eigenvalues of As or Bp equals 2.

span.label: A 2D quantum system with anyonic excitations can act as a quantum computer: unitary gates are performed by braiding excitations around each other, measurement by fusing them.
span.quote: A two-dimensional quantum system with anyonic excitations can be considered as a quantum computer. Unitary transformations can be performed by moving the excitations around each other.

span.label: Fault tolerance is intrinsic and topological: the ground-state degeneracy is protected against local perturbations, so errors are corrected at the physical level.
span.quote: The degeneracy is persistent to local perturbation.

span.label: braiding of anyonic excitations
span.quote: Such motion (“braiding”) can be considered as fault-tolerant quantum computation.

span.label: degenerate ground state (encoded qubit)
span.quote: the degenerate state undergoes a nontrivial unitary transformation when one particle moves around the other

span.label: nonabelian anyons
span.quote: These particles are nonabelian anyons, i.e. the degenerate state undergoes a nontrivial unitary transformation when one particle moves around the other.
